summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure, was admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath. He was found to have elevated cardiac enzymes and BNP, indicating a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and acute on chronic heart failure. A cardiac catheterization revealed a total occlusion of the left circumflex artery, which was successfully treated with a drug-eluting stent. During admission, he experienced transient acute kidney injury likely due to contrast and heart failure, hyponatremia, and episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia managed by his ICD and medication adjustment. He was stabilized on optimized medical therapy including dual antiplatelet therapy, high-dose statin, beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor, diuretics, and digoxin. His symptoms improved, renal function normalized, and he was discharged home with instructions on medication adherence, daily weight monitoring, low-salt diet, and follow-up care.
